name: lilysharp
description: Sheet music from plain text — LilyPond-derived engraving, live as you type.
author: Yoshifumi Tsuda

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_proposeScore
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows the AI's new version of a .lys file beside the score as it stands, to play and to accept or reject.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to write or change a Lily# (.lys) file, instead of editing the file yourself. Give the file's absolute path and, to change a score that is there, `edits`: each `old` a chord, a bar or a line copied from the score as lilysharp_readScore shows it, with its `new`; `all: true` changes every place `old` stands, so one chord revoiced throughout a part is one edit. Do NOT write the whole file again to change part of it. `text`, the WHOLE new text, is for rewriting most of a file; a new piece written with lilysharp_draftScore takes `draft: true` and no text. A NEW piece goes to a new file (name it with lilysharp_checkName), never over a score that is open or attached, unless the musician asks for that file in so many words. Lily# compiles it first: if it has errors they come back and nothing is shown — fix them and call again. Otherwise a new piece (the file empty) is written straight into the file; a change to a score is shown to the musician beside the score as it stands, to play and to accept or reject, and the result says which. Accepted, it is in the editor, not saved: read it with lilysharp_readScore, not from the disk. What to change next, the musician says in the chat; call it again with the edits for that.

file.description: The .lys file's absolute path — for a score open in the editor and not saved yet, the path it is named by.

text.description: The whole new text of the file, for rewriting most of it. Leave it out with `edits` or `draft`.

edits.description: Changes to the score as it stands, in place of its whole text. They apply in order; nothing is shown unless all apply.

old.description: Text of the score exactly as lilysharp_readScore shows it: a chord, a bar, a line or several.

new.description: What stands there instead (empty to remove it).

all.description: true: change every place `old` stands. Without it `old` must be there exactly once.

part.description: With `edits`: a part's name. The edits then change that part's text alone — its own block, its music in each section and the phrases it calls, what lilysharp_readScore shows with `part` — so the same chord in another part is left, and the rest of the score need not be read.

note.description: One or two sentences to the musician about the change, in their language.

draft.description: true: propose the piece written into this file's draft with lilysharp_draftScore, instead of a text given here.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_draftScore
languageModelTools.displayName: Write a new Lily# piece's draft
languageModelTools.userDescription: Writes a new piece into a draft a part at a time, unseen until the AI proposes it whole.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to write a NEW Lily# piece a part at a time before proposing it: one reply that runs long is cut off and lost. Give the new file's absolute path and `text`, the next part of the file (the header and the parts, then a section, then the next, then the form and the score); it is added at the draft's end. `edits` (each `old`, found once in the draft, and its `new`) mend what is there; `restart` begins the draft again. The draft is not shown to the musician and not compiled; the answer says what it holds. When the whole piece is in it, propose it with lilysharp_proposeScore, the same file and `draft: true`.

file.description: The new .lys file's absolute path, as lilysharp_checkName found it free.

text.description: The next part of the file, added at the draft's end.

edits.description: Changes to the draft as it stands: each `old`, copied exactly and found once, becomes `new`. Made before `text` is added.

restart.description: true: throw the draft away and begin it again with `text`.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_readScore
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads a .lys score as it stands in the editor, saved or not.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to read a Lily# (.lys) file before changing it, instead of reading the file from the disk: it gives the text as it stands in the editor — a score not saved yet is not on the disk at all, and a saved one may have changes the disk does not. Give the file's absolute path (for a score not saved yet, the path it is named by). To work on one part, give `part` (its name, as `gtr`): it answers that part alone — its own block, its music in each section and the phrases it calls — a fraction of the score. A long reading comes in pages: the answer says how to read the next (`page`).

file.description: The .lys file's absolute path — for a score open in the editor and not saved yet, the path it is named by.

part.description: A part's name (as it stands after `part`): read that part alone (optional).

page.description: Which page of a long reading, from 1 (optional).

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_reviewScore
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reviews a .lys score as music: its facts, what it does well, and what to look at, for the chat to explain in plain words.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this when asked to review, check or give feedback on a Lily# (.lys) piece, the one open in the editor unless another is named. It answers a report on the score as it stands in the editor, with how to read it first: the piece's facts, what it does well, the compiler's errors and warnings, and findings, each with where it is, why it matters and when it does not apply. The findings are counts, not judgements: explain them to the person in plain words. It changes nothing. Make a fix with lilysharp_proposeScore once the person agrees.

file.description: The .lys file's absolute path. Leave it out for the score open in the editor.

audience.description: Who the review is for, judged from how the person writes; ask if it is not clear. A beginner may not know what a key is.

focus.description: Keep the findings of one theme alone, when the person asks about one.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_writePart
languageModelTools.displayName: Write a part's music by place
languageModelTools.userDescription: Writes music into a .lys score by place — a part's section, some of its bars, a new part — shown beside the score to accept or reject.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to change the MUSIC of a Lily# (.lys) score by place, in place of lilysharp_proposeScore's `edits`: rewrite a part in a section (`write`: part, section, music), several parts or sections in one call, some bars of it (`bars`: "5-8", counted in the section from 1), a singing part's words with its notes (`lyrics`), or add a new part (`newParts`, its music in `write`; a section left out is silent). Nothing of the old text is copied. Write `music` as lilysharp_readScore shows the score (in absolute octaves where it shows them), a bar line after every bar, as many bars as it replaces — as the score's own parts are written: the grammar guide need not be read for this. All of it is placed or none, and what does not fit comes back, every point at once: a part or a section the score has not, bars that cut through a phrase of several bars, a score that would not compile, a bar that does not add up, a section left longer or shorter than the other parts'. A warning the compiler did not give before comes back to you once, unseen; sent again as it is, the change is shown to the musician with the warning. The musician sees the change beside the score as it stands and accepts or rejects it; the answer says what was written where. For a section added or removed, the form, a phrase's own text, or anything that is no part's music, use lilysharp_proposeScore.

file.description: The .lys file's absolute path — for a score open in the editor and not saved yet, the path it is named by.

write.description: The music to write, one item for a part in a section. They are placed together or not at all.

part.description: The part's name, as it stands after `part` — or a new part's, declared in `newParts`.

section.description: The section's name, as it stands after `section`.

bars.description: The bars to replace, counted in the section from 1: "5-8", or "3". Leave it out to write the part's whole section.

music.description: The music, as it stands between the braces of the part's block: notes and bar lines, a phrase the score has by its name. As many bars as it replaces.

lyrics.description: A singing part's words for that section (the text of its lyrics row), written with its notes. Leave it out to keep the words.

newParts.description: Parts the score does not have yet. Each is declared, and given a staff in every score that shows the part it stands after.

part.description: The new part's name: letters and digits, as `str`.

title.description: The name printed at its staff, as "Strings".

short.description: The short name printed from the second system on, as "Str.".

body.description: The lines of its part block, a line each, as the score's other parts have them: `instrument violin` (an instrument's name sets its clef, range and sound), or `clef treble` and `midiInstrument "string ensemble 1"`.

after.description: The part it stands after, in the file and in the scores. Leave it out to stand last.

first.description: true: it stands before every other part, in the file and in the scores (under a chords row) — a voice over a band. Not with `after`.

singer.description: A sung part's singer: `female` or `male` (this machine's default voice), or a voice lilysharp_listVoices gave, in quotes (`"neutrino/MERROW"`); empty for the default voice. Written as `singer … sings on PART`; the part's body names its words (`lyrics words`), and its staff prints them. Leave it out for a part that only plays.

note.description: One or two sentences to the musician about the change, in their language.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_readChords
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads the chord progression of a .lys score, section by section, from what it names and what its parts play.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this before arranging a Lily# (.lys) piece — adding or rewriting a part, revoicing its chords, reharmonizing — to know its harmony, instead of naming the chords from the notes yourself. It answers the progression section by section as a `chords` block, a bar between bar lines, with the form as played, the distinct chords in order (give them to lilysharp_chordVoicings as `chords`) and each part's range. A chord the score names stands as written: a `chords` row, an `@chord(…)`, the chord an `@diagram(…)` shape sounds; the rest is read from the notes, and the answer marks which is which and where a reading is less sure. To rewrite or revoice ONE part, give `parts` with that part (the guitar: `["gtr"]`): the answer is then of the bars that part plays in, its chords still named from every part's notes (the bass says the root of a chord the guitar plays without it), a bass note under it that is another part's left out of the name. Read for a part, the answer also lists each chord as that part writes it (`Bb = <bes, f bes d' f'>`, and in how many places): copy that text into lilysharp_proposeScore's `edits` as `old`, with `part` — the part need not be read for it. It changes nothing.

file.description: The .lys file's absolute path. Leave it out for the score open in the editor.

parts.description: The parts to read, by name (as they stand after `part`). Leave it out to read them all, and the chords rows.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_chordVoicings
languageModelTools.displayName: Find chord voicings a player can hold
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists the voicings of a chord a guitarist, bassist or string player can hold, in a register, as Lily# notes and chord diagrams.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this BEFORE writing a chord for a guitar, bass, ukulele, banjo, violin, viola, cello or double bass part, to know which notes its player can hold — not every stack of a chord's notes can be fingered. Give the chord symbol (Cm7, G7/B, F#m7-5, Bbmaj7), the instrument, the part's sound (its midiInstrument) and the register you want it in (two note names, as C3 and C5 or c and c''). It answers the voicings, commonest first, each as the Lily# chord to write (<c g bes ees' g'>, in absolute octaves) with its chord diagram (x35343); on a distorted sound (overdriven guitar, distortion guitar) its power chords of two or three notes come first, since a full chord blurs there; for a bowed string, the double stops it can sound (two notes at once). Give strings ("1-4": the four highest, 1 the highest) to have only shapes on those strings, the root not always lowest — a band's clean guitar plays its chords there, the bass having the low strings. Give `fromFret` (as 5) for shapes up the neck, no open string. A band's guitar need only keep the root out of the bass's register: for its triads ask `strings: "1-3"` with `fromFret` — full three-note shapes, the root in an upper voice. `omitRoot: true` (the request says "without the root") leaves the root out of seventh and ninth chords, which keep three notes or more; a triad, two notes without it, keeps its root in an upper voice on the upper three strings (or those of `strings`), and the answer marks it — one call serves a progression of both. For several chords, give `chords` (the symbols of the progression, in order) in place of `chord`: it answers ONE voicing for each, chosen so that the hand moves little from chord to chord — one call for a whole part's chords, not one a chord.

chord.description: The chord symbol: Cm7, G7, G7/B, F#m7-5, Bbmaj7, A5 …

instrument.description: guitar (the default), bass, ukulele, violin, viola, cello, doubleBass, or a tuning word (guitarDropD, bass5, …).

low.description: The register's lowest note, as C3 or c (optional).

high.description: The register's highest note, as C5 or c'' (optional).

sound.description: The part's midiInstrument ("overdriven guitar", "electric guitar (clean)" …): on a distorted sound, power chords of two or three notes come first (optional).

strings.description: A fretted instrument's strings to play, by number, 1 the highest: "1-4" (the four highest), "2-5", "1,2,3" (optional). A band's clean guitar: "1-4".

chords.description: A progression's chord symbols, in order, in place of `chord`: one voicing each, the hand moving little between them.

omitRoot.description: true: shapes without the chord's root, which the band's bass plays. A triad keeps its root, in an upper voice on the upper strings.

fromFret.description: The lowest fret a shape may press, no open string then: 5 for the shapes from the fifth position up. Give it when high chords or a higher position are asked for (5, or 7): without it the lowest positions come first.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_listVoices
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists the singing voices available on this machine, by provider, gender or language, with the names a score writes after singer.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this BEFORE writing a singer "…" in a score, to know which voices exist on this machine: never guess a voice's name. With no input it lists them all; give provider, gender or language to narrow it. It answers each voice's name as a score writes it (engine/name), what it calls itself, its gender where it says, and the languages it sings. A voice that does not state its gender is kept when you ask for a gender, and marked so.

provider.description: Only this provider's voices: diffsinger, neutrino or voicevox (optional).

gender.description: Only voices of this gender, and those that do not state one (optional).

language.description: Only voices that sing this language: japanese or english, or ja or en (optional).

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_checkName
languageModelTools.displayName: Check a new Lily# score's name
languageModelTools.userDescription: Says whether a new .lys file's name is free in its folder, or a free one beside it.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this before proposing a NEW piece, to know that its file name is not taken — instead of listing the folder in a terminal. Give the absolute path you mean to use. It says whether a file, or a score open in the editor and not saved, already has that name, and if so names a free one to use instead.

file.description: The new .lys file's absolute path, named after the piece's title.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_readGuide
languageModelTools.userDescription: Gives the AI the Lily# grammar, the guide to composing a new piece, or the path for teaching Lily#.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this before composing music — a piece, a song, a score — or writing or changing Lily# (.lys) text, unless the Lily# instructions are already in your context. Lily# is the music notation language (.lys files) this editor engraves, plays and checks; it is NOT LilyPond. Topic "grammar" gives how Lily# is written; topic "composing" gives how to compose a new piece — its file and first lines, the tool to propose it with, a starting point — and the composing guide; topic "start" gives how a new piece begins without the guide, for a chat that has the Lily# instructions; topic "learn" gives the path for teaching Lily#, from the most useful operations to the advanced, for anyone asking how to write .lys or use Lily#. Asked to compose music here with no file named, compose it in Lily#.

topic.description: "grammar": how Lily# is written. "composing": how to compose a new piece, with the composing guide. "start": how a new piece begins, and its starting point, alone. "learn": how to teach Lily# to someone asking how to write it, in order. "song": how to write a song — a sung part, its words and its singer — over a score that is there (its chords, a recording read into it). "accompaniment": how to arrange accompanying parts — a band, a piano — over the chords of a score that is there.

part.description: Which part, from 1 (the default). A guide comes in parts; each says which part to read next.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_readScan
languageModelTools.displayName: Read a scan into a Lily# score
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads images or a PDF of sheet music into a Lily# score (OMR), opened beside its scan.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this to turn images or a PDF of sheet music into a score — "convert this image to a score", "read this scan", "OMR this PDF" — instead of transcribing it yourself. Give the absolute paths of the files, the pages in order. Lily#'s OMR reader writes a .lys beside them, opens it with its preview and its scan, and marks the bars it doubts with @todo; the result names the file. It may take a minute or more a page.

files.description: The images (png, jpg, …) or PDFs, absolute paths, the pages in order.

languageModelTools.name: lilysharp_fixScanBars
languageModelTools.displayName: Open a scanned score's bars beside the scan
languageModelTools.userDescription: Opens bars of a score read from a scan beside the scan, to mend misreadings there.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this when the musician asks to fix a misreading in a score read from a scan (a .lys with its .omr.json beside it) and names the bars: it opens them beside the scan, where the musician mends them — a bar the reader marked @todo has the AI's reading of it, against the scan, asked for at once. Do not rewrite such bars yourself. Give the file's absolute path and the bars (as numbered in their part, with the part's name) or their lines. With no bar named, ask which, or tell the musician to right-click the bar on the score and choose Edit Bars Beside the Scan.

file.description: The .lys an OMR reader wrote, its absolute path.

bars.description: The bars, as numbered in their part (1 = its first bar).

part.description: The part the bars are in; the first part when left out.

lines.description: Or the bars' lines in the file, 1-based (as Ask AI in Chat's pointer gives them).

semanticTokenTypes.description: Note pitches (c, d, e, f, g, a, b)

lilysharp.preview.openWithScore.markdownDescription: Open a preview beside a `.lys` file when it is opened (not on a tab switch, nor in a diff). An open preview follows the active `.lys` file whatever this says; lock it from its title bar to keep it on one file.

enumDescriptions: The preview is light under a light VS Code theme and dark under a dark one (the default).
Always the printed page: black notes on white, whatever the editor theme.
Always dark: the page inverted to white notes on a dark ground.
lilysharp.preview.theme.description: The score preview's color scheme. Takes effect immediately in open previews.

lilysharp.playback.soundFont.markdownDescription:
**Not used while `#lilysharp.playback.MIDIOutput#` names a port** — the notes go to that port instead (this sound font plays only when the port cannot be opened).

The sound font the preview plays with (the Play button, Alt+P / Alt+M and the auditions): a path to an `.sf2`, `.sf3` or `.dls` file on this machine (also the **Lily#: Choose Sound Font…** command). Empty: the font of the *Lily# Sound Font* extension (installed with Lily#), else the General MIDI bank your computer already has — Windows' `gm.dls`, macOS's DLS bank — or, where there is none, simple oscillator tones. Each part plays the instrument its `midiInstrument` or preset names, as the exported MIDI does. Takes effect in open previews.

**Export as WAV** and **Export as MP3** play the score through this font, as Play sounds it (`.sf2`, `.sf3` and `.dls` alike); only where the preview has no font do they ask for one.

**Shosa** and **Bamen** play their songs with this font too: it is the one sound font setting of the three.

**[Choose a file…](command:lilysharp.chooseSoundFont)**

lilysharp.playback.MIDIOutput.markdownDescription:
A MIDI output port of this machine to play through instead of the preview's own synth — the Play button, Alt+P / Alt+M and the auditions all go there — named as the **Lily#: Choose MIDI Output…** command lists it. **While a port is named, `#lilysharp.playback.soundFont#` is not used**; the port's own instruments sound (if the port cannot be opened, the preview plays with its sound font and says so). Empty: the preview's sound font. On Windows *Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth* plays with no setup; a virtual port (loopMIDI on Windows, an IAC bus on a Mac) carries the notes into a DAW or a VST host, where your own instruments are. Each part keeps its channel and sends its General MIDI program (its `midiInstrument` or preset), as the exported MIDI does; the drums are on channel 10. Takes effect on the next sound.

**[Choose a port…](command:lilysharp.chooseMidiOutput)**

lilysharp.playback.audition.description: Sound notes as you edit: the note the caret lands on, a note as you type it, and what the step keys (Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down, Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown) step a note or a chord shape to. Plays through the open preview, so nothing sounds while no preview is open. Play Note at Cursor (Alt+P) and Play Current Measure (Alt+M) are not affected.

lilysharp.playback.highlightSource.markdownDescription: While the preview plays, light the text of the notes sounding now in the editor — each note, chord, drum stroke and chord symbol as it is heard, in every part at once. The notes are those of the text as it was when Play was pressed: after an edit nothing more is lit until the next Play.

enumDescriptions: The voice is sung again about a second and a half after you stop typing, so it is ready by the time you press Play. The engine runs between pauses in your typing, never during them.

The voice is sung again only when you press Play (that Play plays the instrument; the next one sings). For a slow engine — a DiffSinger voice on the CPU — where singing after every pause would keep the machine busy.
lilysharp.playback.prepareSinging.markdownDescription: When the sung voice is prepared after the lyrics or the notes change. The microphone over ▶ is grey and still while a voice is not sung yet, pulses while the engine sings it, and turns blue when it is ready; a Play meanwhile plays the part's instrument.

lilysharp.export.videoEncoder.markdownDescription: The `ffmpeg` program **Export as MP4** encodes the video with (Lily# does not bundle one). Empty: `ffmpeg` found on your `PATH`. Install it from [ffmpeg.org](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) — on Windows `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`, on a Mac `brew install ffmpeg`, on Linux your package manager — or name the program's full path here.

lilysharp.editing.typingAids.markdownDescription: Typing aids in `.lys` music: an octave mark, a duration digit, a dot, a string number (`\`) or an annotation (`@`) typed anywhere on a note moves into its slot on that note; a digit always leaves a valid duration (`c1` + `2` → `c2`, `c4` + `6` → `c64`; 5, 7, 9 and 0 leave the note unchanged); `<` `>` `(` `)` `[` `]` `~` keep chords, slurs, beams and ties paired and on their notes. In a page's text (a ```md fence): Enter on a list item begins the next one and on an empty item ends the list, and `*`, `_` or a backtick typed over a selection surrounds it. Off: every key is typed exactly as pressed. Ctrl+Shift+Up / Ctrl+Shift+Down are not affected.

lilysharp.editing.flatSpelling.description: How flat pitches (E♭, A♭) are spelled in the autocomplete list. Both spellings always compile; this only changes which the completer suggests.

lilysharp.ai.editModel.markdownDescription:
The language model Lily#'s own features that change the music use — *Lily#: Rewrite with AI…* (the command palette) and *Fix OMR Marks with AI…*: a model id or family from **Lily#: Select AI Model…**. Copilot's chat — *Ask AI in Chat* (Ctrl+I) and *Compose with AI…* — uses the model picked in the chat instead. Empty chooses automatically — the largest model on offer, passing over the small ones (mini, nano, lite, …), which write poor Lily#. Ghost Completion has its own: `#lilysharp.ai.ghostModel#`.

**[Choose a model…](command:lilysharp.selectAiModel?%5B%22edit%22%5D)**

lilysharp.ai.ghostModel.markdownDescription:
The language model Ghost Completion uses: a model id or family from **Lily#: Select AI Model…**. It answers as you type, and VS Code drops a suggestion the moment the caret moves, so it needs a FAST model — a large one is cancelled before it shows. Empty chooses automatically: a small model (mini, nano, lite, …).

**[Choose a model…](command:lilysharp.selectAiModel?%5B%22ghost%22%5D)**

lilysharp.ai.ghostCompletion.markdownDescription:
Suggest the next measure as ghost text while you type (just after a barline), using your language model (GitHub Copilot). Each suggestion is compiled first and only shown if it is valid. Off by default because it calls the model as you type.

It is an inline suggestion, and Lily# turns inline suggestions off in `.lys` files by default (`editor.inlineSuggest.enabled`), because GitHub Copilot's own completion slowed every keystroke there. When you switch this on, Lily# offers to turn inline suggestions on for `.lys` files and to keep Copilot's completions off there (`github.copilot.enable`).

enumDescriptions: Before a recording is converted without words beside it (`<name>.lrc`), ask whether to fetch them from LRCLIB (lrclib.net): the song's title, artist and length are sent, only when you choose to.
Never ask and never fetch: a `<name>.lrc` you put beside the recording is still read.
lilysharp.recordings.fetchLyrics.markdownDescription: Whether **Convert Recording to Lily# (.lys)…** offers to fetch the song's words from LRCLIB before it converts. The chart then has the words under the sung line (Orecchiante 0.17.0 and later; Japanese words for now).

lilysharp.scans.verifyOnSave.markdownDescription: When a `.lys` read from a scan (its `x.omr.json` beside it) is saved, have the OMR reader engrave it again and compare it with the scanned pages, bar by bar; the scan view and the `@todo` quick fixes then show what still differs. Takes a few seconds; needs a reader that has `omr verify`.

lilysharp.fonts.folders.markdownDescription: Folders to look for SMuFL music fonts in, before the standard SMuFL locations: a font's metadata (`<name>_metadata.json`) and program (`.otf`) directly in a folder or in a subfolder of its name. A score names its font only (`fonts { music "MyFont" }`); this says where this machine keeps it. The environment variable `LILYSHARP_FONT_PATH` is read too (by the command line as well).

walkthroughs.title: Have Lily# sing a score
walkthroughs.description: From nothing installed to a voice singing your words: the extension that sings, an engine for it, and a first song.

steps.title: Install the Cantoria extension
steps.description:
Voices are sung by Cantoria, a separate free extension that drives a singing engine on this computer.
[Install Cantoria](command:lilysharp.installCantoria)

steps.title: Upgrade the Cantoria extension
steps.description:
Cantoria is installed, and a newer version of it is out. Voices are sung by Cantoria, a separate free extension that drives a singing engine on this computer.
[Upgrade Cantoria](command:lilysharp.upgradeCantoria)

steps.title: Set up one singing engine
steps.description:
Download one engine as the page on the right says, then tell Cantoria where it is. One is enough. An installed VOICEVOX, and OpenUtau's voices, are found for you.
[Find Engines on This Computer](command:cantoria.findEngines)
[Choose DiffSinger Voices Folder](command:cantoria.chooseVoicesFolder)
[Choose NEUTRINO Folder](command:cantoria.chooseNeutrinoFolder)
[Choose VOICEVOX Folder](command:cantoria.chooseVoicevoxFolder)

steps.title: Check that a voice is ready
steps.description:
Cantoria says which voice would sing, or what is still missing.
[Check Setup](command:cantoria.checkSetup)

steps.title: Open a first song and play it
steps.description:
A song you know, with its words and a singer line. Open its preview and press Play.
[Open a First Song](command:lilysharp.openFirstSong)
With an NVIDIA GPU it is the whole song; without one, its opening, which a voice on a processor sings in a minute or two. Either can be opened: [the whole song](command:lilysharp.openFirstSongWhole), [the short one](command:lilysharp.openFirstSongShort).

walkthroughs.title: From a song to a dance
walkthroughs.description: A song written in Lily#, sung by a voice and danced by a character with Shosa, then a video of it.

steps.title: Write a song
steps.description:
A score with words and a singer line. Have the AI compose one, or give a song to a score you have: one read from a recording keeps its bars and chords, and the recording plays under the song — or, with an accompaniment arranged from its chords, the recording goes silent and the score's own band plays.
[Compose with AI…](command:lilysharp.composeWithAiInChat)
[Write a Song over These Chords…](command:lilysharp.writeSongOverChords)
[Arrange an Accompaniment…](command:lilysharp.arrangeAccompaniment)

steps.title: Have a voice sing it
steps.description:
The words are sung by a voice on this computer. Its steps are a walkthrough of their own; once a voice is ready, the preview's Play sings the song.
[Set Up a Singing Voice](command:lilysharp.setUpSingingVoice)

steps.title: Put a dance on it
steps.description:
Shosa, a free extension, dances a score: its Add a Dance… asks for a character for each singing part and what kind of dance, and Copilot's chat writes the dance beside the score.
[Add a Dance…](command:lilysharp.danceWithShosa)
[Install Shosa](command:lilysharp.installShosa)

steps.title: Make a video
steps.description:
In the dance's preview, press Play to watch it. Pick 16:9, or 9:16 for Shorts, in the preview's header, then export the video with the song's sound.
[Export MP4 Video…](command:shosa.exportVideo)
